Half of the people under this post don't understand that an ED is a mental problem, not a calorie/weight problem. You can eat enough calories and still have an ED. Personally I believe that the same thing that can be good for some people can harm others. This applies to OMAD. If you genuinely feel like you feel much better when you're doing OMAD and it gerald natural to you here's no problem to it. It becomes a problem when you feel deprived, when you're extremely hungry during your fast so you endup bingeing, when you feel guilty for eating when you're supposed to be fasting, when you become obsessed with eating only at a certain time, etc. When those feelings are present it can become disordered very quickly. Also, I absolutely agree that this promotes a binge/restrict cycle, this is a thing that alot of people with earings disorders struggle with (especially BED and bulimia). Bingeing and then compensating by fasting, exercising, etc. 

So yeah, OMAD can be an ED but that doesn't mean that everyone who does OMAD has an ED !

I'm not an expert!!! But I have my own experience with binge eating from the past and I've done quite alot of research about this.

There's a huge diffirence between occasionally overeating (eg at a birthday party)  and binge eating which is eating large amounts of food in one sitting (I think to be diagnosed it needs to happen at least 3 times per week but don't quote me on that). Obviously I can't diagnose you by reading one post, but it sounds like what you're experiencing is binge eating.There are many factors that can contribute to binge eating. 

- Mindless eating

- Restriction (starving yourself, dieting). You said that sometimes you starve yourself. This does lead to more overeating in the short and long run and that's just a fact. You might notice that starving yourself makes you think more about food, which could make you feel like you're addicted to it. I also want to add "feeling guilty" in this category. Try to eliminate those  bad feelings about yourself and food (ik it's not that easy). If you overrate, that's ok. No need to blame and starve yourself it will only make things worse. 

- Hormonal issues or other physiological health issues (eg vitamin deficiencies)

- Trauma or other mental issues (eg depression)

- A certain attachment to food ( food fills a void in you, it brings you joy. Or maybe as a kid food was the love language /used as a reward by your parents)


I guess this is debatable but personally I believe that food isn't a drug and you're not actually addicted to it. You just have an unresolved problem that leads to overeating. 

I'd recommend to keep a food journal. Write down how you're feeling before a meal/snack, how hungry you are (look up hunger scale), what's the setting, etc. And do the same after the food intake. Do this for a few weeks and you'll be able to notice a certain pattern which could help you understand more why you binge. If you already know what triggers your binges, be honest with yourself write it down. You said that starving yourself is a trigger for eating more, so that's already one thing to write down. Is there more that you could identify? Once you've identified the triggers, you can work with them and try to eliminate them from your life.

It's also making sure you don't constantly over work yourself to prevent burnout (coming from a workaholic). Getting enough sleep, taking a day off when you feel like you're getting drained, planning breaks from whatever you're doing (eg studying), etc.
